- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eulsa Treaty made Korea a protectorate of Japan, giving Japan control over Korean foreign affairs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eulsa Treaty granted Japanese officials extraterritorial rights in Korea.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eulsa Treaty sparked widespread protests and unrest in Korea.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Korean emperor, Gojong, protested the treaty and sought international support to overturn it.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eulsa Treaty was ratified by the Japanese parliament in December 1905 and went into effect in February 1906.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eulsa Treaty marked the beginning of Japanese colonial rule in Korea.
